notes: Carrington's regard is already tested four times before N03 on the shared nodes; this line adds only the warning after N02, then spends T2N01 and T2N02 on the two arcs the shared nodes never touched, Lavinia and the widow, each with an active attempt that costs time while the cart comes nearer. After T2N03 the three closing opportunities (the valet's hour, Millicent's cloak, the Major's dictated account) set where each resolution lands at T2N04, and Nathaniel's scrap after T2N01 tells the player early whose hand carried the tallow, so the wrong passenger is chosen knowing.

minor_nodes.title: The Chair Outside the Door
minor_nodes.summary: The Major sets Fairbrother on a hall chair outside the nephew's locked room and says, not to you but over your head, that the housekeeper walks the rounds tonight; if she brings back the house's hour she goes in the account, and if not the solicitor has another word for her.
minor_nodes.image: a hall chair set square against the nephew's door, a candle on the floor beside it
who: Reginald Fairbrother (the master's valet of forty years)

minor_nodes.title: The Scrap Under the Door
minor_nodes.summary: In the linen press you unfold Nathaniel's scrap, pencil pressed hard enough to tear: yard, twenty to eleven; one light going up the back stair, servants' tallow by the colour; a man's cuff on it, not a sleeve. Tell them. The hand that carried the stub was never a lady's.
minor_nodes.image: the words 'a man's cuff' pressed through the paper

minor_nodes.title: Pails on the Back Stairs
minor_nodes.summary: Lavinia passes you on the back stairs with coal and two pails, sent to lay the study fire alone, the grate still holding its ash. Above, the Major stands at the gallery rail with his watch open. She slows at the turn and looks back to see whether you will come.
minor_nodes.image: a coal scuttle set down on the stair, its handle still swinging

options.do: Tell her to wait on the landing; you will go into the study with her when the Major has done with you
options.effect: she sets the pails down and waits, and the cart's hour runs on while the Major keeps you at the rail

options.do: Nod her on into the study alone and keep your place beneath the Major's watch
options.effect: she goes in with the pails; the door shuts on her and the ash

options.do: Go up past her into the study and rake the grate yourself before she can lay the fire
options.effect: either you have the ash pan in your hands when the Major calls you down from the gallery, or his voice halts you on the threshold; either way she has seen you come for her, and he has seen you climb

tell.how: when you come into the kitchen with snow on your skirts, Lavinia either moves up the bench to make room for you or turns her shoulder and keeps talking to the cook

minor_nodes.title: Praise on the Gallery
minor_nodes.summary: Cordelia Ormsby, dressed now and languid against the newel, tells the Major that his housekeeper is the most discreet creature she has met in a country house. The Major's watch is still open. She says it to him and looks at you, and waits for what you will do with it.
minor_nodes.image: the widow's hand lying open on the newel post, palm up

options.do: Curtsey and say the gallery carpet was swept clean this morning, madam
options.effect: she inclines her head; the hairpin and the keyhole are closed between you

options.do: Ask her, before the Major, whether she slept at all, having been so long in the cold on the gallery
options.effect: her hand closes on the newel; the Major's eyes go from her to you

tell.how: at the ice house either the widow's own maid comes wading down with your shawl, sent by her mistress, or nobody comes and your skirts freeze stiff

minor_nodes.title: Whose Window, Whose Boots
minor_nodes.summary: The doctor straightens from the body and asks, in the same flat voice he uses for weather, whether the lady whose window it was knew whose boots went out of it. Ellingham's pen waits. The Major's boots stand in the gun room still, the snow line dried white on the leather.
minor_nodes.image: a dried white tide line across the ankle of a riding boot

options.do: Say the window and the boots are all you can speak to, and that a housekeeper does not know what ladies know
options.effect: the doctor nods as if that were the whole answer; the keyhole at midnight stays yours

options.do: Tell him she was at the study keyhole at midnight and heard the ward in the Major's room on her way there
options.effect: Ellingham writes it; the doctor says he will have to put it to her

options.do: Go back for the Major's boots and carry them down to the ice house so the doctor can read the snow line himself
options.effect: either you come back with the boots under your shawl and the doctor turns them to the light, or the groom meets you in the gun room with the Major's orders and you come back empty; in both cases you have been seen carrying the Major's things across the yard

tell.how: when you take your place before the fire, the widow has either drawn her chair to the Major's side with her fan up or sits with her hands folded, watching you as a woman watches a servant she has decided to keep

minor_nodes.title: The Kitchen's Tongue
minor_nodes.summary: You come in from the snow to find Lavinia at the kitchen table telling the cook you left her to the study alone, and that the Major has been asking what went out of the grate. Her hands are grey with ash to the wrist. The kitchen goes quiet when it sees you.
minor_nodes.image: ash grey to the wrist on a housemaid's hands

options.do: Say before the kitchen that you sent her to the grate alone and whatever went out with the ash is the housekeeper's fault
options.effect: the cook's eyebrow goes up and the kitchen will carry it to the Major by dinner, but Lavinia's hands stop shaking

options.do: Say she was told to wait on the landing and did not
options.effect: the kitchen turns back to her, and the cook says what kitchens say about girls who do not wait

options.do: Take your tea without a word and go up
options.effect: the talk starts again behind you before the door is shut

tell.how: Lavinia brings the lamps into the drawing room before the house gathers, and either sets a lit candle at your elbow without being asked or leaves you to find your own light

minor_nodes.title: The Master's Chair by the Fire
minor_nodes.summary: Fairbrother has laid the drawing room for the hearing without being told: the master's chair drawn to the fire for the Major, the sherry decanter gone from the sideboard, Lavinia sent in with the lamps. Forty years of service, turned in an afternoon toward whoever sits at the head.
minor_nodes.image: the pale ring on the sideboard where the sherry decanter stood
who: Reginald Fairbrother (the master's valet of forty years)

minor_nodes.title: The Hour Not Asked
minor_nodes.summary: In the passage after the room has emptied, Fairbrother stands with Nathaniel's key in his hand, waiting to be told whether to turn it. You are alone with him for the first time since the box. He has kept silent for you; he is waiting to learn what it bought.
minor_nodes.image: the nephew's door key held flat on the valet's palm
who: Reginald Fairbrother (the master's valet of forty years)

options.do: Ask him only whether Mr Yardley will come down to dinner or have a tray sent up
options.effect: he answers the question you asked and turns the key; the hour stays his

options.do: Ask him what hour he lit the Major up the back stairs that night
options.effect: he says the stair was dark by eleven, which is not an answer, and does not turn the key until you have gone

options.do: Tell him the box was one short and you both know whose cuff carried it
options.effect: he says the box is his to count, and that he counted it before you came to this house

tell.how: at the sideboard he either sets your tea things out with the linen folded the way you asked or stands behind your chair where you cannot see his face

minor_nodes.title: The Cloak in the Hall
minor_nodes.summary: Millicent waits in the hall for the carriage, her cloak not yet brought, the Major's greatcoat on the stand with the wrapped glass weighting one pocket. Nathaniel is still locked above. She asks you, without turning, whether the glass goes down the road with her.
minor_nodes.image: the Major's greatcoat sagging on one side from the weight in its pocket

options.do: Tell her the study at ten was a settlement, not begging, and that you will say so at the magistrate's if you are asked
options.effect: she turns and looks at you for the first time since the drawing room

options.do: Say nothing and go to fetch her cloak
options.effect: she lets you put it on her as if you were a hook on the wall

options.do: Go to the greatcoat and take the glass out of the pocket before the Major comes down
options.effect: either you have it in your apron when his step sounds on the stair and must put it back under his eye, or his hand is on the coat before yours and he buttons it, saying your surname once; in both cases Millicent has seen you reach

tell.how: at the carriage step she either stops and says she had asked you as a woman, or goes out without a cloak and lets her eyes pass over you as over furniture

minor_nodes.title: The Account Read Back
minor_nodes.summary: Before the carriage, the Major dictates the household's account to Ellingham at the library table and has you read it back: the quarrel at eleven by his watch, the lady's candle, nothing of the key. The solicitor's pen is wet. He asks whether that is how the house remembers it.
minor_nodes.image: the Major's watch lying face-up beside the solicitor's wet page

options.do: Read it back as dictated, eleven by his watch, and say that is how the house remembers it
options.effect: he nods to Ellingham and the page is sanded

options.do: Read it back with half past ten where he has eleven, and the back stairs dark by eleven
options.effect: Ellingham's pen stops; the Major says the housekeeper is tired and the page stands as dictated

tell.how: at dinner the study key either comes across the table to you on his open hand or stays on his chain, and he speaks your surname to the room or does not speak it at all

minor_nodes.title: Locking the Study
minor_nodes.summary: You lock the study at night with the Major's key, or watch him lock it with his own. Fairbrother carries the last candle down the back stairs, counts the box without looking, and either bids you goodnight by name or lets the dark take the question of the hour with him.
minor_nodes.image: the study key turning in a lock you did not break
who: Reginald Fairbrother (the master's valet of forty years)

minor_nodes.title: Tea Without the Bell
minor_nodes.summary: The widow's door is shut, her own maid inside dressing her hair, or open with her voice calling your name for a pin. Below, Lavinia either brings your tea unrung and whispers that the grate is relit and nobody has asked about her candle, or sets it down and goes.
minor_nodes.image: a cup of tea set down on the housekeeper's table, steam rising in a cold room
